blocklisted.KJVPCE: King James Version: Pure Cambridge Edition

reasons.KJVA: Apocrypha edition of KJV/KJVPCE; Marginalia does not support Apocrypha. See scripts/near-duplicate-report.json (excluded from generate:scrollmapper output).
reasons.KJVPCE: Not a meaningful variant of KJV, a 98.5% match.
reasons.OEBcth: A 98.5% match to OEB. Same translation project (Open English Bible), two spelling locales. Diffs are almost entirely American vs Commonwealth orthography (fulfillment/fulfilment, neighbor/neighbour, splendor/splendour). Neither is more “authoritative”; US-spelling OEB is the default most digital catalogs surface first, and Marginalia’s UI/docs lean US English.
reasons.VulgConte: A 98.1% match to VulgHetzenauer. Both are Clementine Vulgate printings, not different translations. Michael Hetzenauer’s early-20th-century edition is a well-known scholarly reconstruction of the Clementine text (1592/93/98). Conte’s is a later public-domain digital update that says it is based primarily on Hetzenauer — so Conte is the derivative, Hetzenauer is the source lineage. Diffs look like spacing/compounding (quam ob rem vs quamobrem, id est vs idest), not content. Same pattern as “specialized reprint of the main text.”
reasons.SpaRVG: Licensing: Explicitly forbids reproduction for profit; CrossWire lists CC BY-NC-ND. Free church printing is allowed; a commercial SaaS is not.
reasons.GerLeoNA28: Licensing: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (verlag causa mundi). NC blocks commercial use.
reasons.MKJV: Licensing: Not worth the hassle to maintain license.
